# OA.5 Numerical checks {#num}

Section 4 of the paper computes date-specific Markov policy functions by backward induction along the demographic
transition, and selects among the candidate equilibria at each state; the technical documentation
[@BergGE26doc] gives the algorithms and the code. This chapter reports two checks of that computation.

## OA.5.1 Date-specific and stationary policies {#num-stationary}

The gap between the date-specific solution and a time-invariant policy function, the approximation of much of the
quantitative politico-economic literature, at the same dates. Section 4 summarizes it in a footnote.

{{< include _generated/groups/num-stationary.qmd >}}

## OA.5.2 Equilibrium selection {#num-selection}

For every file of results behind an exhibit, the largest number of equilibria and of candidate solutions found at
any state, and the number of states at which the solver fell back on its default. A single equilibrium at every
state means that the selection rule of section 4 never had to choose.
